finalText:
Found it. `engine.js` was rounding to 2 decimals right after the percent coupon and again after the flat coupon, before converting to the order's currency. That's rounding twice instead of once.

It only showed up when a percent coupon was in play and the currency wasn't USD — the early rounding shaved a fraction of a cent off the USD amount, and converting that trimmed number to GBP, CAD, or JPY landed one cent (or one yen) low. USD orders never triggered it since there's no conversion step to expose the drift.

Fixed by letting the coupon math run on the full-precision USD amount and rounding only once, after conversion — matching how the finance team expects it to work. All 40 tests pass now.
